newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia says only UN can order troops into Albania.
newsitem.headline: Russia says only UN can order troops into Albania.

text.p: The Russian foreign ministry, cautioning against premature European intervention, stressed on Monday that foreign troops should be sent to Albania only if the United Nations Security Council ordered it.

"Whether for police duties or for any other purpose, (international forces can be sent to Albania) only on the basis of a U.N. Security Council resolution," Deputy Foreign Minister Alexander Avdeyev told Interfax news agency.

"That is our firm position and we do not intend to deviate from it," he added, stressing that discussions within the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) on sending troops had so far been only on a "hypothetical level".

European Union foreign ministers agreed on Sunday to send a small assessment team to pave the way for a larger advisory mission on civilian reconstruction and police and military matters. The assessment team was due in Albania on Monday.
On Friday, the OSCE envoy to Tirana, Franz Vranitzky, said he saw no alternative to Western military intervention to halt the anarchy and chaos that has gripped the country.
But at the EU meeting in the Netherlands, Britain, Germany and Sweden opposed sending a multinational force in response to requests from beleaguered President Sali Berisha.
The United States also said on Saturday it was not ready to join a proposed stabilisation force in Albania for the moment.

On Thursday, the Security Council appealed to Albanians to stop violence and cooperate with diplomatic efforts to reach a peaceful solution to the crisis. But it made no reference to the call from Albania's beleaguered government for military help.
Russia, permanent member of the Security Council and of the OSCE, has sent peacekeeping troops to the former Yugoslavia.
Moscow evacuated much of its diplomatic mission from Tirana aboard U.S. military helicopters on Saturday.

Avdeyev said "everyone who should leave has left". Twelve embassy staff, including ambassador Igor Saprykin and the consul, were left in Tirana. Moscow had no word of some 240 other Russian citizens scattered throughout the country.
